newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: SBC Warburg launches NZ bond, bank bill indices.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg launches NZ bond, bank bill indices.

text.p: Investment Bank SBC Warburg on Monday launched a group of New Zealand bond and bank bill indices, which it said provided comprehensive coverage of the New Zealand market by issuing sector, maturity classes and risk profile.
The indices were developed with the help of fund managers, asset consultants and institutional investors.

The family of indices will be comprised of Composite, Government, Corporate Group A (minimum credit rating A-/A3), Corporate Group B (rated BBB+ and below), Corporate Composite, Inflation-linked and Bank Bill indices.
There will also be sub-maturity indices available where appropriate for 1-plus year, 0-3 year, 0-5 year, 3-7 year 5-plus year and 7-plus year maturities on each of the indices.

The bank said the indices were similar to the SBC Warburg Australia bond and bank bill indices launched 10 years ago. The Australian indices had become recognised as an industry standard, with 90 percent of fund managers using them to monitor their performance.
New Zealand market players would have a reliable benchmark against which to measure the performance of local debt markets.

"Depth of market coverage, timely production, and accurate, reliable underlying data have increased the stature of the Australian bond and bank bill indices over time," said Sharon Mitchell, head of rates sales with SBC Warburg Australia.
She said those same characteristics would lead to the New Zealand indices becoming an equally valuable tool for investors in the New Zealand market.
